bonds.fealty: a lord to a liege: pays a share of its taxes up, sends levies when called, is protected in return
bonds.tribute: an outlaw power to a stronger one: pays a share of its take to be left alone and backed
bonds.client: paid work for another power; no obedience; either side can end it
bonds.member: an order, guild or council seat inside a people's own structure
bonds.recognized: a seat whose claim the Council of Mavens has evaluated and recorded

the_accords.what: a covenant between peoples, not a government: signatories open one craft to anyone; any signatory may suspend its accord against a people that wronged it

the_quiet_house.what: the one roof under which no people may raise a hand; where powers at war can meet

council_of_mavens.what: the primary body that promotes the middle way through what it does. It evaluates; it does not rule, tax or levy. Its power is credibility.

members.rule: each people or sovereign power may send a maven; Warden Coll sits for the Radiant Plateau's Edge District

council_of_mavens.source: canon: warden_coll ('evaluates rather than decides'); nexuses.json (the ninth, unbuilt nexus at the Council of Mavens, made of friction; its corruption, evaluation-as-avoidance, is Erik's to rule)

proposedFunctions.recognition: Credibility, not command. A seat taken by force is held either way; a holder the Mavens recognize is seen as legitimate by the peoples who lean to the middle and by the Accord's signatories (their standing toward the holder rises a step), and the seat's own ground regards the holder one step better. That is why anyone with a seat wants it.
proposedFunctions.arbitration: Two powers in dispute can bring it to the Mavens instead of the field. A ruling moves both powers' standing with every signatory.
proposedFunctions.record: The Mavens record Accord suspensions and breaches, which makes them dated world events.

council_of_mavens.theNexusHook: The ninth nexus is built when the Council meets a real edge and does not withdraw — when it rules on something hard. A player who forces a ruling (the Slip, a taken crown) is building it.

blocs.what: The unaligned settlements already ask things of each other in writing, and Millbrook's panel counts written settlement requests as mandate (Dresh's first condition). That custom is the whole Compact today: no oath, no host, no seat. A player who gets the free places to promise each other more makes it real.
